entries.title: Amos 8:1
segments:
Summer fruit; such as the fig, which was harvested in the latter part of summer. 
 
vv 1-3. 
 
Though God is long-suffering, not willing that any should perish, his forbearance has a limit; and when this is reached, his wrath will destroy without remedy.

entries.title: Amos 8:2
segments: The end is come upon--Israel; like the fruit in this basket, they are ripe for the harvest.  In the original, the two words rendered "summer fruit" and "end" are similar, as if it were said, "A basket of ripe fruit;" "my people Israel is ripe for the end."

entries.title: Amos 8:5
segments: New moon; one of the holy days, in which secular labor was suspended.  Compare

. 
 
  The ephah; the measure used in selling their grain. 
 
  The shekel; the weight of money received in return.

The Sabbath was made for man, and all good men love its holy rest.  But they who are intent upon unrightous gain must be expected to hate the interruption which it brings to the pursuit of mammon, and to use their influence against its sanctity.

entries.title: Amos 8:6
segments: Buy the poor; for servants.  See

entries.title: Amos 8:7
segments: When the rich and powerful oppress and spoil their fellow men, and no earthly tribunal can be found to maintain the cause of truth and justice, God himself will interpose in behalf of the poor and defenceless, and thrust down their oppressors from the height of their prosperity into remediless ruin.

entries.title: Amos 8:8
segments: Rise up; with water; that is, be covered.  Compare

, where the sluggard's field is said, in the Hebrew, to be "all risen up with thorns." 
 
  Shall be cast out; its inhabitants shall be carried away by the flood.

entries.title: Amos 8:11
segments:
vv 11-12. 
 
  The words of the Lord; in their distress they shall seek counsel from God, but receive no answer.

vv 11-14. 
 
When men will not listen, in the time of their prosperity, to the messages of God's word, they shall seek from him in their calamity some message of comfort, but receive no answer; then all their vain confidences will fail, and they perish with none to help them.

entries.title: Amos 8:14
segments: Thy god--Beersheba liveth; that is, "As thy god, O Dan, liveth;" "The manner of Beer-sheba liveth."  These are forms of swearing.  "The manner of Beer-sheba" is the idolatrous form of worship there established.
